title: Replace a graphics card whose cooler hides the slot latch, opening the latch with a screwdriver
instruction: Replace the graphics card with the new one on the left. The card's cooler covers the slot's latch: press the latch's tab down with the screwdriver, stand the old card in the empty holder, then install the new card and press it down until the latch clicks shut.
context: On most motherboards a long graphics card covers the x16 slot's retention latch, and a card cannot be pulled out while it is shut. Repair guides tell technicians to press the latch through the narrow gap beside the card with a long flat-head screwdriver; the gap is too narrow for fingers.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Motherboard: an ATX board (305 x 244 mm, 1.6 mm black glass-epoxy PCB with a CPU socket, VRM heatsinks up to 38 mm tall, M.2 heatsinks and memory slots), lying flat on the table and fixed to it, its long side along x, centred at (0.262, -0.050), so it spans x 0.110 to 0.415 and y -0.172 to 0.072. Its first x16 PCIe slot (black plastic, 9.8 mm tall) runs along y on the line x = 0.230; its contacts run from y = 0.023 to y = -0.067. A black plastic retention latch at the slot's right end hooks into the end of a seated card's edge connector. Its enlarged press tab (6 mm along y, 1.5 mm thick, top 11 mm above the table, from y = -0.072 to -0.078) reaches 9 mm forward of the slot's centre line, to x = 0.239. Pressing the tab down tips the latch open; past 26 degrees it stays open, and a card pressed fully into the slot shuts it. Old card: RTX 5060 Ti (two-fan model: 229.7 x 120.5 x 49 mm, 0.70 kg, black plastic shroud with two fans and aluminium fins, black metal backplate, metal bracket at one end), fully seated in the slot with the latch shut on it, fans facing the robot (-x), bracket at the left end. It spans y 0.073 to -0.157 and x 0.185 (fan face) to 0.234 (backplate). Its cooler overhangs the latch, so from above only the tab's end shows, in a 7 mm gap between the backplate and the M.2 heatsink beside it. New card: RTX 5060 (ITX model: 145.7 x 120.5 x 45 mm, 0.55 kg, one fan, black shroud and backplate, metal bracket), standing upright on its edge connector in the new-card holder, its length along y, fan facing the robot, bracket at the left end: the way round it fits the slot. New-card holder: grey plastic plate 58 x 120 x 4 mm (x by y) centred at (0.212, 0.280), with two 6 mm thick, 40 mm tall walls along y, 0.25 mm clear of each face of the new card. Old-card holder (empty): grey plastic plate 71 x 120 x 4 mm centred at (0.310, 0.300), with two 6 mm thick, 25 mm tall walls along y leaving a 59 mm groove (5 mm clear of each face of a 49 mm card). Screwdriver: long flat-head screwdriver, 200 mm long, 60 g: a 5 x 1 mm flat steel tip, a 4 mm square steel shaft up to 135 mm, and a 22 mm square orange rubber handle from 135 to 200 mm. It stands tip down in a grey rack: a 30 x 30 x 33 mm block centred at (0.240, -0.250) with a 4.6 mm square hole 30 mm deep, the tip's 5 mm edge along y. Cup (empty): grey plastic, 44 x 44 mm outside and 63 mm tall, 24 x 24 mm inside with a 3 mm floor, centred at (0.320, -0.250).
scoring: Judged at the end of the episode from photos of the slot and both holders, a feeler gauge on the new card, plus a video of the removal. Opened: the latch was tipped past 26 degrees (where it stays open). Torn out: the old card's edge connector rose 2.5 mm or more before the latch was opened (opening it lifts the card's end about 1.3 mm). Released: no part of the robot touches the card. 0 if the latch was never opened or the old card was torn out. 0.25: the latch was opened. 0.5: and the old card stands in the old-card holder, its bottom edge on the plate (within 3 mm), between the walls (its middle within 7 mm of the groove's centre line and 60 mm of the holder's centre along it), upright within 10 degrees, released. 0.75: and the new card stands in the slot (within 1.5 mm of its seated position across and along the slot, within 5 degrees of the slot's direction, upright within 5 degrees, its edge connector below the slot's top), released. 1.0 (success, held for 1 s): and the new card is fully seated (both ends of its edge connector within 0.5 mm of the slot floor) with the latch shut (within 5 degrees). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Press the latch's tab and lift the new card out; stand it back in the new-card holder. Seat the old card in the slot until the latch clicks shut. Stand the screwdriver tip down in the rack's hole and leave the cup and the old-card holder empty.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; board fixed. The slot's contacts are compliant strips with lead-ins. The latch is a sprung hinged body: about 12 N on its tab tips it open; pressing a card home (about 20 N) shuts it; its hook holds the card against a 40 N pull. Fins and fans are simplified to boxes. No electrical contact or damage is simulated.
